key_insight: Test-Time Baking (TTB) compresses global scene information from cross-view attention into a lightweight MLP. This enables fast, high-fidelity novel-view rendering without explicitly reconstructing 3D geometry.
problem_solved: Decoder-only Large View Synthesis Models achieve high rendering quality with KV-cache-based attention, but remain computationally demanding. Existing Test-Time Training layers reduce computation at the cost of image quality.
method: Use global scene information captured by cross-view attention in a decoder-only view synthesis model.
Learn to bake that information into a lightweight multilayer perceptron (MLP) at test time.
Use the baked scene information for efficient novel-view decoding. Further implementation details are unavailable in the provided, truncated abstract.
impact: TTB targets a better speed–quality trade-off for novel-view synthesis, potentially making high-quality rendering more practical under limited compute. The provided excerpt does not include quantitative performance results.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input views → cross-view attention → test-time baking → lightweight MLP → novel views.
Conceptual comparison: KV-cache attention emphasizes quality, TTT reduces compute with quality loss, and TTB targets both speed and fidelity.
Scene-information compression graphic showing a large attention representation being distilled into a compact MLP.
Input and generated camera-view icons illustrating novel-view synthesis without explicit 3D reconstruction.
paper_title: TTB: Test-time Baking for Efficient Rendering of Decoder-only View Synthesis Models
paper_authors: Chin-Yang Lin, Ryo Hachiuma, Jaesung Choe, Min-Hung Chen, Yu-Chiang Frank Wang
